chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who bequeathed thirty dinars so that a man from among our companions might be emancipated with it, but none was found for that amount.
He عليه السلام said: "A person should be purchased from among the people and then emancipated."

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: our companions, meaning the Shia community in context
key_terms.أَوْصَى: made a bequest in his will
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ دِينَارًا: thirty dinars designated for the bequest

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a bequest to free one of the companions cannot be carried out as specified?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a bequest designated for freeing a member of the Shia community when such a person cannot be found for the specified amount. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the purpose of manumission should still be fulfilled by purchasing and freeing someone from among the people generally.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5501 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who bequeathed thirty dinar for the emancipation of a man from among our companions, but no such person was found.
Imam (as) said: "A person should be purchased from among the people and then emancipated."
